required_floor_classes.lane_definition: A science/energy/environment scenario cannot pass if access to research infrastructure, energy service, environmental protection, public lands/recreation, water services, or community protection falls below reviewed component-specific floors.

A science/energy/environment scenario cannot pass if lower costs are achieved by degrading research quality, energy reliability, energy security, emissions performance, pollution control, ecosystem condition, water quality, or worker/community safety.

A science/energy/environment scenario cannot pass if access loss, affordability burden, pollution exposure, energy insecurity, climate risk, or research opportunity shifts by income, geography, race/ethnicity, tribal status, disability, or environmental-justice status without review.

A science/energy/environment scenario cannot pass if research capacity, grid resilience, energy security, ecosystem resilience, climate adaptation, water resilience, or pollution-response capacity falls below reviewed floors.

A science/energy/environment scenario cannot pass without separate science, energy, and environment component paths; state/local and tax-expenditure scope; implementation cost; innovation lag; grid and ecosystem transition risk; and delivery feasibility.

science_energy_environment_specific_floo.definition: Research investment, infrastructure access, knowledge outputs, mission continuity, and workforce capacity require sourced floors before a science component scenario can pass.
Energy reliability, affordability, security, resilience, emissions, and transition-risk floors require sourced values before an energy component scenario can pass.

Pollution control, ecosystem condition, water quality, public lands, recreation, climate resilience, and community protection require reviewed floors before an environment component scenario can pass.
Energy burden, pollution exposure, climate risk, tribal/rural access, environmental justice, and research-opportunity distribution require reviewed floors.
No target cost can be selected without state/local and tax-expenditure scope separation for science, energy, and environment.
No composite target can be selected; separate science, energy, and environment policy paths, implementation costs, transition risks, and delivery feasibility are required.

public_warning_phrases: This science/energy/environment floor packet defines required floor concepts, but it does not set threshold values or pass/fail findings.
The composed FY2025 subtotal is not one OMB function, one program, one performance surface, or one composite target.

No lower-cost science/energy/environment scenario is admissible until separate science, energy, and environment component paths and access, quality/safety, equity, adequacy/resilience, and delivery-feasibility floors are thresholded, sourced, reviewed, and passed.
No composite target, target cost, federal effect, gross savings, net savings, solver input, department-cut instruction, technology-savings claim, or balanced-budget claim is populated.
No FOIA request, records request, form, email, phone call, or agency/person contact was submitted.

This record is not outcome-floor passage, not a composite target, not a component policy path, not state/local scope, not tax-expenditure scope, not a federal score, not a target-cost selection, not solver input, not a rate calculation, not a public rate card, not a savings estimate, not a waste finding, not a fraud finding, not a department-cut instruction, not a technology-savings claim, and not a balanced-budget claim.
